name: Krang Suri Falls
description: Iconic turquoise waterfall near Amlarem in West Jaintia Hills, famous for its vivid blue-green waters, natural swimming pool, and short forest trek. One of Meghalaya's most photogenic spots.
facts: Located about 30 km from Jowai and 90 km from Shillong.
Entry fee around ₹50; life jackets available for swimming.
Best visited October to April for clearest water.
Short 15-20 minute trek from parking.

name: Dawki and Umngot River
description: Border town on the India-Bangladesh frontier famous for the crystal-clear Umngot River where boats appear to float in mid-air. Features the historic British-era suspension bridge.
facts: Umngot River is among India's cleanest rivers.
Dawki Bridge built by the British in 1932.
Boating popular especially in dry season (Nov-Mar).
Integrated Check Post for trade with Bangladesh.

name: Shnongpdeng
description: Riverside village upstream of Dawki on the Umngot River, known for camping, kayaking, cliff jumping, and quieter pebble beaches away from the main border traffic.
facts: About 8 km upstream from Dawki.
Popular for overnight riverside camps and adventure sports.
Clearer and calmer water compared to Dawki ghat.
Local operators offer guided activities.

name: Nartiang Monoliths
description: Largest concentration of megaliths and menhirs in Meghalaya, erected by Jaintia kings and clans between the 16th and 19th centuries. Includes the tallest menhir in the region.
facts: Declared of national importance; largest single collection in Khasi-Jaintia Hills.
Tallest menhir erected by Mar Phalyngki commemorates a victory.
Located north of Nartiang market; open site.
Linked to the summer capital of the Jaintia kingdom.

name: Nartiang Durga Temple
description: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where the left thigh of Sati is believed to have fallen. Ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Jayanti (Durga), blending Jaintia and Hindu traditions.
facts: Approximately 600 years old; associated with Jaintia kings.
Shakti known as Jayanti, Bhairava as Kamadishwar.
Major pilgrimage site especially during Durga Puja.
Located in Nartiang village, about 25 km from Jowai.

name: Thadlaskein Lake
description: Historic man-made lake (also called Pung Sajar Nangli) beside NH6 near Mukhla village, created according to legend by Sajar Nangli and his followers. Popular picnic and boating spot.
facts: Located about 10 km from Jowai and 58 km from Shillong.
Folktale attributes its creation to digging with bow tips.
Sacred site for local Niamtre community in the past.
Easily accessible on the Shillong-Jowai highway.

name: Jowai
description: Headquarters of West Jaintia Hills district and cultural hub of the Pnar (Jaintia) people, situated on a plateau surrounded by the Myntdu River. Gateway to many attractions in the district.
facts: Elevation around 1,365–1,380 m.
Population about 28,430 (2011 Census).
Important education and business center for the district.
Home to markets, churches, and starting point for day trips.

name: Tyrshi Falls
description: Scenic multi-tiered waterfall near Jowai off NH6, accessible via a short walk across an arch bridge over paddy fields. Offers views of cascading water and surrounding valleys.
facts: About 5–8 km from Jowai town.
Named after a local warrior in legend.
Short walk from the road; views from upper and lower levels.
Less crowded alternative to more famous falls.

name: Thlu Muwi Stone Bridge
description: Historic megalithic stone bridge built by Jaintia warriors under royal orders for the king's passage over the Muwi stream. Accompanied by nearby waterfalls.
facts: Located about 16 km from Jowai on the road to Dawki.
Built with large hewn granite slabs on pillars.
Constructed to facilitate travel from Jaintiapur to Nartiang summer capital.
Nearby Muwi Waterfalls add scenic value.

name: Ialong Park
description: Ecological park and sacred grove about 8 km from Jowai, offering panoramic views of the Pynthorwah Valley and Myntdu River. Features walking trails and natural settings.
facts: Developed with tourism infrastructure including facilities.
Overlooks beautiful valley landscapes.
Includes elements of local sacred forests.
Popular for family outings and photography.

name: Syntu Ksiar
description: Picturesque riverside valley and picnic spot on the Myntdu River near Jowai, meaning 'golden flower'. Site of historical significance related to freedom fighter Kiang Nangbah; features a suspension bridge.
facts: About 7 km from Jowai.
Historical site of the freedom struggle against the British.
Popular local picnic and angling spot.
Suspension bridge across the river.

name: Phe Phe Falls
description: Hidden two-tiered waterfall near Shkentalang village, requiring a short trek through meadows and forest. Known for turquoise pools and relative seclusion.
facts: About 20–30 km from Jowai; near Krang Suri route.
Name means 'paradise' in local language.
15–20 minute hike from trailhead; local guide recommended.
Best October to April; avoid heavy monsoon.

name: Shillong
description: Capital of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the 'Scotland of the East' for its pine-covered hills, colonial charm, and pleasant climate. Major cultural and educational hub with markets, churches, and access to surrounding attractions.
facts: Elevation around 1,496 m.
Named after the deity Lei Shyllong.
Major base for exploring East Khasi Hills.
Connected to Guwahati by NH-6.

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1,965 m, located 10 km from Shillong city. Offers panoramic views of the city, surrounding hills, and countryside; sacred site for local Khasi traditions with a shrine to U Lei Shyllong.
facts: Highest point in the state.
About 10 km from Shillong.
Popular for sunrise and sunset views.
Accessible by road with short walk.

name: Elephant Falls
description: Three-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, about 12 km from the city center. The mountain stream cascades through fern-covered rocks in successive drops, easily accessible and popular for short nature visits.
facts: Original Khasi name Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew.
About 12 km from Shillong on Cherrapunji road.
Three successive falls.
Surrounded by lush greenery.

name: Ward's Lake
description: Historic man-made lake in central Shillong, also known as Nan Polok, named after Sir William Ward. Features gardens, a footbridge, boating, and a peaceful setting near the Raj Bhavan.
facts: Located in the heart of Shillong.
Man-made in the late 19th century.
Popular for boating and walks.
Surrounded by gardens and pathways.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Historic town and plateau in East Khasi Hills, once considered the wettest place on Earth. Gateway to major waterfalls, caves, living root bridges, and viewpoints overlooking the Bangladesh plains.
facts: Elevation about 1,430 m.
Traditional name Sohra.
Base for Nohkalikai and other attractions.
Holds records for extreme rainfall.

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m (1,115 ft), near Sohra. Fed by plateau rainfall, it plunges into a green pool with a tragic local legend associated with the name.
facts: Height approximately 340 metres.
About 5 km from Sohra.
Best viewed in monsoon for full flow.
Named after legend of Ka Likai.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters)
description: Seven-segmented waterfall near Mawsmai, dropping about 315 m over limestone cliffs. Spectacular during monsoon when segments merge; offers views toward the plains.
facts: Also known as Seven Sisters Falls.
Height around 315 metres.
Near Mawsmai Cave.
Best in rainy season.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Accessible limestone show cave near Sohra with lit passages, stalactites, and stalagmites. One of the first tourist caves in the region, about 150 m long and suitable for general visitors.
facts: About 6 km from Sohra.
Lit show cave approximately 150 m.
Rich in calcite formations.
Near Nohsngithiang Falls.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Iconic two-tiered living root bridge in Nongriat village, grown from rubber tree roots by Khasi communities over generations. Requires a challenging trek of about 3,500 steps from Tyrna; UNESCO tentative list related.
facts: Located in Nongriat village near Sohra.
Approximately 180-200 years old.
Trek from Tyrna involves ~3500 steps.
Unique stacked double-decker structure.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Widely known as Asia's cleanest village, near the India-Bangladesh border. Features living root bridges, bamboo skywalk, meticulously maintained lanes, and community-led conservation in a matrilineal Khasi setting.
facts: About 90 km from Shillong.
Declared cleanest village in Asia in 2003.
Home to single living root bridge at Riwai.
Near Bangladesh border.

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic canyon viewpoint about 25 km from Shillong, offering sweeping views of deep valleys, cliffs, and rolling hills. Features a steep descent of stone steps to remote villages below.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong near Smit.
Meaning 'end of the hills' in Khasi.
Popular for panoramic valley views.
Steep trail of thousands of steps.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Ancient sacred grove protected by Khasi traditions for centuries, about 25 km from Shillong. Home to rare plants, old-growth trees, orchids, and biodiversity; entry requires a local guide with strict no-removal rules.
facts: About 25 km from Shillong.
Protected by local deity beliefs.
Guided treks only; nothing to be removed.
Rich in epiphytes and endemic flora.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures (Museum)
description: Premier museum in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artifacts, textiles, and traditions of Northeast India's indigenous communities across seven floors and multiple galleries.
facts: Located in Mawlai, about 4 km from central Shillong.
Inaugurated around 2010.
Focus on Northeast indigenous cultures.
Unique hexagonal multi-storey building.

name: Arwah Cave
description: Limestone cave near Sohra known for fossilized marine remains, spacious chambers, and relatively fewer crowds than Mawsmai. Short forest walk from the entrance.
facts: Near Sohra/Cherrapunji.
Features visible fossils in walls.
Less crowded alternative to Mawsmai.
Part of Meghalayan Age Caves tentative sites.

name: Moopun Waterfalls
description: Scenic 110-foot waterfall on the Umjhai River at Mutong village, featuring a rare stone bridge above the falls, natural swimming pool below, and pitcher plants growing on the rocks. Short walk from the road with picnic spots.
facts: Height about 110 feet, width 50 feet.
About 25 km from both Jowai and Khliehriat.
Stone bridge (Moopun) spans the river above the falls.
Legend links it to the Water Goddess from Umhang Lake.

name: Umhang Lake
description: Largest natural lake in Jaintia Hills, located at Bataw village. Formed according to legend when an old woman scratched the earth for water; surrounded by forests and revered by local communities.
facts: About 29 km from Khliehriat.
Also known as the Secret Lake in some accounts.
Sacred to local Pnar communities with annual offerings.
Connected by all-season road via Rymbai.

name: Krem Liat Prah
description: Longest natural cave in India and South Asia, with over 34 km of explored passages on the Shnongrim Ridge. Features vast chambers like the Aircraft Hangar; expedition caving only with guides.
facts: Explored length approximately 34 km and growing.
Located near Shnongrim and Larnai villages.
Requires organised caving trips; not a casual walk-in.
Part of the Abode of the Clouds Expedition surveys.

name: Rynji Falls
description: Roaring waterfall near Cham Cham village, about 3 km south of Mutong. Features hard rock formations, stepping natural ponds above the falls, and forest trails for eco-trekking.
facts: Near Cham Cham village in East Jaintia Hills.
Accessible via footpaths and pedestrian bridges.
Popular for angling and nature walks.
Best in monsoon for full flow.

name: Umbyrlein Falls
description: Iconic waterfall in Rangad Village, East Jaintia Hills, about 36 km from Jowai. Offers scenic cascades amid forested surroundings for nature and photography.
facts: Located in Rangad Village.
About 36 km from Jowai.
Part of local tourism circuit with Moopun and Rynji.

name: Sahksaw Fish Sanctuary
description: Tranquil community fish sanctuary at Cham Cham village, 700 metres from the road. Scenic spot for observing protected fish in clear waters amid picturesque surroundings.
facts: Located at Cham Cham village.
Community-managed conservation site.
Short walk from the main road.

name: Borghat Temple
description: Historic brick temple in Borghat Village dedicated to Lord Shiva, built by Jaintia ruler U Bor Kuseiñ who embraced Hinduism. Features carvings and stands near the old palace ruins.
facts: About 49 km from Khliehriat.
Associated with early Hindu influence on Jaintia kings.
Brick construction with unique carvings.

name: Tisang River
description: Scenic river near Borghat village, about 50 km from Khliehriat, surrounded by forests and villages. Popular for riverside camping and quiet nature experiences.
facts: Approached from Borghat village.
Surrounded by forests.
Hotspot for riverside camping.

name: Lukha River and Bridge
description: Lukha River flowing through mountainous landscape toward Bangladesh, crossed by the longest bridge in the district at Sonapur, about 40 km from Khliehriat. Concrete arch bridge connecting to Assam.
facts: About 40 km from Khliehriat.
Longest bridge in the district.
River flows toward Bangladesh.

name: Moolamylliang Village
description: Village in Saipung Block known for adventure and scenic beauty, offering recreational and natural experiences in a less-visited part of East Jaintia Hills.
facts: Located in Saipung Block.
Promoted for adventure and nature tourism.
Relatively unexplored.

name: Khliehriat
description: Headquarters of East Jaintia Hills district, a coal and limestone mining area serving as the main base for exploring the district's waterfalls, caves, and lakes. Features local markets and connectivity via NH-6.
facts: District headquarters since 2012 split.
Elevation around 1,167 m.
On NH-6 connecting to Assam and other parts.
